title: Pin comment claims a broken re-pricing branch would "FLIP to m2" — the verified broken behavior is the route VANISHING (count 0), contradicting the PR body's own bite proof
detail: With re-pricing disabled, dist[res]=10 via per-pipe relaxation but min_cost[res→m1]=20: 5+20=25≠10 and 10+10=20≠10 both fail the equality test — the route VANISHES (count 0), never flips. Reproduced via toggle; PR body says "vanished entirely". Comment contradicts it.
recommended_fix: Reword comment (a): with first-seen cost both neighbors fail `dist[ns] + min_cost[ns] == dist[u]` (25≠10, 20≠10) — the route vanishes, count 0, matching the PR body's documented toggle proof.

title: New pin dereferences hops[int(off)] unconditionally after the non-fatal count==1 check — the bite failure mis-reads an adjacent slot's Hop (or could panic) instead of surfacing the pinned message
evidence:
testing.expectf(t, count == 1,
	"the re-priced fat bundle must win UNIQUELY (count 1), got %d", count)
testing.expectf(t, s.routing.hops[int(off)].node == m1,
	"next hop must be m1 (bundle priced at its min member: 5+5=10), got %d — the bundle edge was NOT re-priced",
	s.routing.hops[int(off)].node)

testing.expectf(t, s.routing.hops[int(off)].pipe == s.topology.pipe_id[rep_slot],
	"representative Hop.pipe must stay the LOWEST-SLOT member (pipe %d, tier narrow), got %d",
	s.topology.pipe_id[rep_slot], s.routing.hops[int(off)].pipe)

	return r.hop_offset[idx], r.hop_count[idx], true
detail: expectf records and continues; with count==0, off=hop_offset[idx]=set_start reads hops of another (u,d) slot (or past the end → panic). The PR body's bite output shows mis-reads: "got 3" (host id), "got 2" (m1→host pipe). Same shape as r1 note 3.
recommended_fix: Guard the node and pipe asserts with `if count == 1 { ... }` so the recorded count message is the failure, not a mis-read or panic — as r1 note 3 prescribed for the sibling pins.
